Skalat Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ternopilska oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Skalat's Jewish community, documented from 1613, became independent in the late 17th century and peaked at 3,256 people (55.2 percent of the town) in 1890, before pogroms in the 1880s and 1900s drove many to emigrate to the US. On the first days of the German occupation in July 1941, local Ukrainians staged a pogrom that claimed 560 lives. This cemetery was demolished in the 1950s, according to local residents, and a soccer field was built on the site; a lapidarium with preserved gravestones, presumably moved during the stadium's construction, was established adjacent to it in 2002.
